objective: 验证：神经网络的泛化行为能否作为 bootstrap 解空间刚性的探针

input_params.description: The hypothesis proposes a percolation-based relationship between Ca/Si/Al/O composition, structural void density, and ion migration activation energy in glass. This requires a materials design exploration across compositional space. I will generate a series of glass network compositions, simulate their atomic structures using MD to quantify void density and ion migration barriers, and identify the percolation threshold where activation energy changes abruptly. The goal is to map composition → void density → activation energy and validate the percolation mechanism.
input_params.expected_prediction: The exploration will reveal a critical composition threshold (e.g., CaO/SiO2 ratio ~0.3) where void density percolates and activation energy drops sharply by ~0.5 eV. Compositions below this threshold will show high activation energy (>1.0 eV) and isolated voids; above it, lower activation energy (<0.6 eV) with connected void networks. The relationship will follow a power-law near the threshold consistent with percolation theory.

input_params.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Execute a classical MD simulation on Ca-Si-Al-O glass to generate ion migration trajectories and compute temperature-dependent diffusivity, which will be used to test the non-Arrhenius hypothesis and extract activation energy parameters. This requires the md_pipeline skill with packing_tool and lammps_tool.
input_params.expected_prediction: The simulation will produce diffusivity values D(T) at multiple temperatures (e.g., 300K, 600K, 900K) showing non-Arrhenius behavior (curved Arrhenius plot), with apparent activation energy increasing at lower temperatures due to network connectivity effects.
